questions.stem: What key question do marketing attribution data models seek to answer?
options: How much budget each department should receive
Which channels and touchpoints contribute significantly to the final sale
Which product has the highest profit margin
How many employees the marketing team needs
Which customers should be removed from the mailing list
questions.explanation: When running campaigns across many channels, the key question attribution models address is which channels and touchpoints contribute significantly to the final sale.

questions.stem: What is the main limitation of single-touch attribution models?
options: They require machine learning expertise
They cannot be used for e-commerce
They overlook the cumulative effect of multiple interactions, giving a limited view of overall effectiveness
They need external economic data
They only work for TV advertising
questions.explanation: Single-touch models are simple but overlook the cumulative effect of multiple interactions, limiting the view of the overall marketing strategy's effectiveness.

questions.stem: Which attribution model credits all sales to the final marketing touchpoint before a purchase?
options: First click
Linear
Time decay
Last click
U-shaped
questions.explanation: Last click credits all sales to the last marketing touchpoint before the purchase, whether an ad click, an email or a referral link.

questions.stem: Which attribution model attributes the sale entirely to the touchpoint that initially attracted the customer's attention?
options: Last click
Time decay
Linear
W-shaped
First click
questions.explanation: First click attributes all sales to the first marketing touchpoint that attracted the customer, emphasising initial interactions and long-term customer value.

questions.stem: Which businesses are said to be best suited to single-touch attribution models?
options: E-commerce stores with short sales cycles and straightforward paths to purchase
B2B enterprises with long buying cycles
Service-oriented businesses with complex journeys
Businesses using many channels simultaneously
Businesses seeking to model external economic factors
questions.explanation: Single-touch models suit businesses like e-commerce stores with short sales cycles where a single interaction has a big influence.

questions.stem: In the linear attribution model, how is credit distributed?
options: All credit goes to the last interaction
Each touchpoint in the customer's journey receives an equal share of credit
Credit increases for interactions closer to conversion
Credit goes mainly to the first and last interactions
Credit is assigned by a machine learning algorithm
questions.explanation: In the linear model every interaction, regardless of its position in the journey, receives an equal share of credit for the sale.

questions.stem: In the time decay attribution model, which interactions receive the most credit?
options: The first interaction only
Interactions in the middle of the journey
Interactions that occur closer to the conversion
All interactions equally
Interactions on paid channels only
questions.explanation: In time decay, interactions closer to the conversion receive more credit, while earlier touchpoints receive progressively less as their influence decays.

questions.stem: How does the W-shaped model differ from the U-shaped model?
options: It gives all credit to the last click
It ignores the first interaction
It uses statistical analysis of historical data
It further emphasises intermediate touchpoints between the first and last interactions
It assigns equal credit to every touchpoint
questions.explanation: The U-shaped model credits the first, last and some middle interactions; the W-shaped model further emphasises the intermediate touchpoints.

A model that credits only the first click
A position-based model for B2B
A rule that gives equal credit to every channel
A data-driven model using statistical analysis of historical data, including external factors, to measure each channel's impact on overall sales
questions.explanation: MMM applies statistical analysis to historical internal and external data (sales, spend, economic indicators, seasonality, competition) to quantify each channel's contribution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the multi-touch attribution models described?
options: Last click
Linear
Time decay
U-shaped
W-shaped
questions.explanation: Last click is a single-touch model; the multi-touch models are linear, time decay and position based (U-shaped and W-shaped).
